title: Cavatelli with Beans
subtitle: Small shell pasta in a thick borlotti bean and tomato broth
excerpt: A southern Italian dish of pasta cooked together with borlotti beans in a light tomato broth. Some of the beans are crushed to thicken the liquid. Simple and very filling.
sourceNotes: Pasta e fagioli with cavatelli is a classic of Puglia and Basilicata in southern Italy. Borlotti beans are traditional.

recipe.batchNotes: Make a larger batch of the bean base and cook fresh pasta to order. The base keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The bean broth can be made a day ahead. Add the pasta only when ready to serve.

content.text: Cavatelli with beans is halfway between a soup and a pasta dish. The pasta cooks directly in the bean broth, so the starch thickens the liquid naturally. Serve it straight away as it thickens further as it sits.
Heat the oil in a large pot over a medium heat. Add the onion and celery. Cook for 8 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic, rosemary sprigs, and chilli flakes if using. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until the tomato darkens slightly.
Add the beans. Crush about a third of them against the side of the pot with a spoon. This thickens the broth.
Pour in the stock. Add the salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes. Remove the rosemary sprigs.
Add the pasta directly to the pot. Cook over a medium heat, stirring often, until the pasta is al dente. The broth will thicken considerably.
Check the seasoning. Ladle into bowls. Finish with a generous drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and parmesan if using.

items.symptom: The dish has thickened to a solid mass.
items.cause: It was left to sit too long or the heat was too high during cooking.
items.fix: Stir in a ladleful of hot water or stock to loosen it. Serve immediately after cooking.

items.symptom: The pasta is undercooked after the stated time.
items.cause: Cavatelli is thicker than most dried pasta and takes a couple of minutes longer.
items.fix: Keep simmering and taste every minute. Add more stock if the pot dries out before the pasta is done.

items.cause: Insufficient salt or stock that is too weak.
items.fix: Season generously at the end and add a squeeze of lemon or a small drizzle of strong extra virgin olive oil.
